text: Fill in the missing key terms of ammonia metabolism and the urea cycle.
questions: The transfer of an amino group to alpha-ketoglutarate, forming glutamate, is called *transamination* and requires pyridoxal phosphate as coenzyme.
Brain and muscle fix free ammonia onto glutamate, and it travels safely in the blood as the amide *glutamine*.
The rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle, CPS-I, requires the allosteric activator *N-acetylglutamate/NAG* to function.
Each molecule of urea carries two nitrogen atoms: one from free ammonia and the other from *aspartate*.
The *fumarate* released from argininosuccinate connects the urea cycle directly to the TCA cycle.

overallFeedback.feedback: Transamination collects amino groups on glutamate, and glutamine synthetase adds free ammonia to glutamate (using ATP) to make glutamine for safe transport; the urea cycle's rate-limiting step (CPS-I) requires N-acetylglutamate activation; the second urea nitrogen comes from aspartate; and fumarate release connects the urea and TCA cycles — an integration point frequently tested in examinations.
